scope: Stateless null/zero/full/random/urandom device descriptions, original shared pseudo inode cache, worker/native byte and positioned I/O, metadata, lifetimes and portable Unix rights.
method: Four independent processes each perform 1,000 checked fixed-work iterations, four Trames vCPUs and three unprofiled counterbalanced before/after samples. Final compilation, local Linux CI and FFI acceptance finish before timing; native Linux runs first on the existing six-vCPU ARM64 environment using the identical static musl ELF, then is stopped during Mac timing. Device cases open/read/write/pread/pwrite/readv/writev/seek/fstat/close each iteration and validate EOF/zeros/counts/ENOSPC/character type. Existing null-device rights case includes open/send/close/recv/alias read/close. Socketpair and an added ordinary positioned-file read/write workload are controls. File setup/cleanup is outside its loop timer. Native macOS uses its own device APIs: null/zero seek returns 27 for the fixture request while Linux returns zero, explicitly checked per platform. macOS provides no full device here, and unprivileged urandom writes return EPERM, so those rows have no macOS throughput substitute. Existing Trames RNG write behavior remains acknowledged discard; native Linux executes native entropy-device semantics. Longest-child loop and whole-process wall medians include different work and are recorded separately. Different kernels/APIs/filesystems/CPU counts make native numbers contextual, not whole-app, Firefox, physical-iPad or universally native-speed claims.

resources: original inode/device behavior with five kinds and both native/worker interfaces
eight cold worker opens share one actual cached inode and distinct real OFDs
renamed mknod device and live readonly/nodev policy plus original mount retained after namespace copy
actual access/modify/open/final-close notifications after alias, worker release and numeric FD reuse
concrete access/synchronous results and raw versus positioned readonly error precedence
scalar/vector/positioned ABI, bad offsets, bad guest buffers and original accepted OFDs
dynamic pseudo controls remain owner-bound through aliases
validation.reuse: Full VFS/kernel/product/FFI passes and production binaries reused after the final Linux cfg(test)-only ABI matrix addition. Only the affected Apple/Linux ABI and strict checks rerun for that addition. Unchanged CPU/memory/graphics acceptance and guest artifacts reused.
validation.environment: Initial compiler ENOSPC recovered by removing only generated incremental caches in known target directories. Final debug checks use CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; release build settings are unchanged. Sources, rootfs, logs, measured baselines and installed stable app were retained.

implementation.identity: Immutable device behavior in the original inode; original full shared OFD, mount, status and close notification. No path-name device bypass.
implementation.pseudo: Only the actual Send+Sync Arc-backed inode cache crosses into the private PathQueries island. Its BTreeMap and u64 identity allocation share a short cache guard; hits release it before content updates, fixed device hits need no content rewrite. Runtime/task Rc/control state stays private.
implementation.io: Original device algorithms and common access/mount/timestamp/notification behavior for owner/native and workers; raw/positioned admission uses compile-time paths and preserves original error order. No additional native permission policy or storage/file-size charge.
implementation.rights: Actual device OFDs are portable SCM_RIGHTS; queued rights preserve full original descriptions and final-close ownership across numeric reuse.
implementation.hot_path: Byte I/O acquires no pseudo cache lock or name lookup. Ordinary CPU/memory/Unix paths gain no global resource lock, service thread, bus, polling loop or memory fence.

remaining: Dynamic/privileged device controls, native-service adapters and Unix-bearing owning graphs
Native TCP/UDP batches, legacy PTY/task/job-control and pending task signals
io_uring controls, mount/nsfs topology and proc controls
Structural file/VM/task transitions and residual whole-process cohort joins
Continue consolidating FD routing/admission to avoid repeated membership lookups; the added file control has no observed material timing regression
